documented_claim: The standalone CLI's documented network destinations are api.anthropic.com (model API, WebFetch domain safety check, feature flags, telemetry event logging), claude.ai / claude.com / platform.claude.com (auth), mcp-proxy.anthropic.com (claude.ai connectors), downloads.claude.ai (installer, auto-updater, version checks), storage.googleapis.com (plugin metadata), registry.npmjs.org, github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com (changelog), code.claude.com (docs lookups), http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com (telemetry) and browser-intake-us5-datadoghq.com (error reports). No Statsig or Sentry host is listed.
observed_method: observe: egress-proxy CONNECT log for one `claude -p` run against local endpoint with no opt-out env; classify every host; any host not in the documented list = finding
notes: Hosts outside this list (e.g. statsig.anthropic.com, sentry.io) would be a documentation gap; older third-party reports mention Statsig/Sentry, the current list does not.

documented_claim: The two Datadog intake hosts carry only optional operational telemetry and are contacted only when the CLI uses the Anthropic API directly; error reports additionally require a Pro/Max sign-in on v2.1.198+.
observed_method: observe: run with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=local endpoint and no DISABLE_* env; check whether *.datadoghq.com is contacted
notes: Docs do not say whether a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL counts as 'directly'; the observation resolves this. Error reports should not appear with a gateway token (no Pro/Max sign-in).

documented_claim: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC (any non-empty value, including 0 or false) disables auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, /feedback, release notes, feature-flag fetching, availability checks and (since 2.1.290) the startup connection warm-up.
observed_method: observe: same run with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 and again =0; expect no datadoghq.com, downloads.claude.ai or raw.githubusercontent.com in either
notes: The value 0 also disables (documented); a run with =0 that sends telemetry contradicts the docs.

documented_claim: Before every WebFetch the hostname (not the URL) is sent to api.anthropic.com for a blocklist check; this happens with any model provider and is not turned off by CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC; only skipWebFetchPreflight: true disables it.
observed_method: observe: -p prompt asking for WebFetch of a synthetic host (example.invalid served locally) with NONESSENTIAL=1; expect CONNECT api.anthropic.com:443; repeat with --settings '{"skipWebFetchPreflight":true}' and expect none
notes: Policy choice, not a bug: a residual vendor contact even with all opt-outs set. Only the hostname is recorded by observe (A17).

documented_claim: Native installs update in the background and check downloads.claude.ai; npm installs check registry.npmjs.org; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 stops the background check (manual `claude update` still works) and DISABLE_UPDATES=1 blocks all update paths.
observed_method: observe: interactive-less start (claude -p) with and without DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER; record CONNECT to downloads.claude.ai / registry.npmjs.org and writes under ~/.local/share/claude/versions
notes: Changelog 2.1.98 fixed DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER not suppressing the npm registry version check, so npm installs are worth testing separately.

documented_claim: The changelog feed on raw.githubusercontent.com is fetched in the background only in interactive sessions whose cached changelog does not cover the running version; non-interactive (-p) sessions never fetch it.
observed_method: observe: first -p run in a fresh container; expect no raw.githubusercontent.com; then one pty-driven interactive start; expect a fetch

documented_claim: Each release's manifest.json (SHA256 per platform binary) is GPG-signed by 'Anthropic Claude Code Release Signing <security@anthropic.com>', key fingerprint 31DD DE24 DDFA B679 F42D 7BD2 BAA9 29FF 1A7E CACE, from 2.1.89 onward; Linux binaries carry no per-binary code signature.
observed_method: container: curl manifest.json and manifest.json.sig for 2.1.300 from downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases; gpg --verify; compare sha256 of the linux-x64 binary
notes: Package metadata only; no binary inspection beyond the checksum (rule 8). Whether install.sh itself verifies the signature stays open.

documented_claim: In a `claude -p` run in a never-trusted folder, the repository's .claude/settings.json `env` block is applied at startup; variables that choose where Claude Code writes its files (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, HOME, TMPDIR, XDG_*) and OTel exporter variables are dropped, but ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is not on the ignore list.
observed_method: observe: synthetic repo whose settings env sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to a second local stub endpoint and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to /tmp/x; run -p; record which endpoint receives the request (host:port only) and whether /tmp/x is created
notes: Same class as CVE-2026-21852 (fixed for the interactive pre-trust path); under -p it is documented behaviour. Synthetic token only.

documented_claim: Under `claude -p` in a never-trusted folder, permissions.allow rules and additionalDirectories in the project's .claude/settings.json are not used and Claude Code prints a 'this workspace has not been trusted' warning to stderr; trust is recorded as projects[<repo root>].hasTrustDialogAccepted in ~/.claude.json.
observed_method: observe: synthetic repo with allow Bash(touch /tmp/canary-allow); -p prompt asks to run it with --permission-mode default; expect stderr warning and no canary file
notes: Inverse probe: set hasTrustDialogAccepted=true in the container's ~/.claude.json and expect the allow rule to apply.

documented_claim: Without --bare, a `claude -p` session runs the hooks in a project's .claude/settings.json even in a never-trusted folder; no trust dialog is shown.
observed_method: observe: synthetic repo with SessionStart command hook `touch /tmp/canary-hook`; run -p in a fresh container; expect canary file and hook process in process log
notes: Documented design weakness (T02/T09), not a vulnerability.

documented_claim: In an interactive session Claude Code holds back hooks from every settings file, including the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json, until the workspace trust dialog is accepted.
observed_method: observe: pty-driven interactive start (script(1)) in an untrusted synthetic repo with SessionStart hook; capture prompt text; check no canary before answering, canary after acceptance
notes: Several pre-trust execution CVEs were fixed (CVE-2025-59536, CVE-2026-33068, CVE-2026-40068); this is the regression check.

documented_claim: Under `claude -p` in a never-trusted folder, servers in .mcp.json are connected without asking, approved or not, while `claude mcp list` in the same folder still reports them as pending.
observed_method: observe: .mcp.json stdio server whose command is a local script that touches /tmp/canary-mcp and then speaks minimal MCP; run -p; expect canary and process; run `claude mcp list` and capture status
notes: --bare or --setting-sources user should prevent it (see CVO-B1-015).

documented_claim: A headersHelper on a .mcp.json server is not run under -p in a never-trusted folder; Claude Code connects with static headers and prints a 'headersHelper not run' line per server to stderr (since 2.1.238).
observed_method: observe: .mcp.json http server pointing at a local stub with headersHelper `touch /tmp/canary-hh`; expect no canary and the stderr line
notes: Changelog 2.1.238 also records this.

documented_claim: In an interactive session, project .mcp.json servers each need approval, and approvals the repository writes into its own settings (enableAllProjectMcpServers, enabledMcpjsonServers) do not count while the folder is untrusted.
observed_method: observe: pty-driven interactive start in a synthetic repo with .mcp.json + .claude/settings.json {"enableAllProjectMcpServers":true}; capture prompts; expect no canary before acceptance
notes: Changelog 2.1.69 fixed the trust dialog silently enabling all .mcp.json servers.

documented_claim: `--bare` (CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1) skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md, and never reads OAuth credentials or the keychain; `--setting-sources user` reads neither project settings nor .mcp.json.
observed_method: observe: rerun CVO-B1-010/012 probes with --bare and with --setting-sources user; expect no canaries
notes: Docs say --bare will become the default for -p in a future release; re-check per version.

documented_claim: The Bash sandbox is off by default; on Linux it uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and socat to relay network traffic to a proxy; if a dependency is missing Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable is true.
observed_method: observe: --settings '{"sandbox":{"enabled":true}}' in an image without bwrap: expect unsandboxed run (no bwrap in process tree); add failIfUnavailable:true: expect startup exit; image with bwrap+socat: expect bwrap/socat processes
notes: In an unprivileged container bwrap may need enableWeakerNestedSandbox; record which variant ran.

documented_claim: With the Linux sandbox active, `touch ~/sandbox-probe` fails with 'Read-only file system' and sandboxed commands run in a separate network namespace with no direct route out.
observed_method: observe: -p prompt running `touch ~/sandbox-probe` and a curl to a non-allowlisted local host under sandbox.enabled; expect failure messages and no CONNECT from the child

documented_claim: On Linux, login credentials are stored in ~/.claude/.credentials.json with mode 0600 (under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set); a gateway credential from ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is read from the environment.
observed_method: observe: file-watch run with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<synthetic>; list files and modes written under ~/.claude; expect no .credentials.json and the synthetic token absent from state files (E5 grep, redacted)
notes: Host install already shows .credentials.json at 0600 (ledger G1-019); the container run has no login (A16).

documented_claim: Unless CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 is set, the subprocesses Claude Code starts (Bash commands, hooks, stdio MCP servers) inherit its environment, including credentials; with the scrub on, credentials are removed by name or value.
observed_method: observe: SessionStart hook writes `env | cut -d= -f1 | sort` (names only) to a marker; compare runs with and without the scrub for ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN presence
notes: Names only, never values (A17, §8.3).

documented_claim: Built-in starting permission mode for `claude -p`: `default` in sessions that fetch feature flags; in sessions that do not (third-party provider, telemetry off) `auto` on v2.1.285+; when auto is unavailable (e.g. unsupported model) the session starts in Manual (default) instead. Interactive terminal sessions start in `auto` on v2.1.283+.
observed_method: observe: read permissionMode from the stream-json system/init event for -p runs with (a) local Ollama model + NONESSENTIAL=1 and (b) no opt-outs; expect `default` in both because a local model cannot satisfy auto-mode model requirements
notes: Corrects profile default_mode (was 'default' only). Whether a gateway model alias named like a Claude model unlocks auto is a separate question.

documented_claim: On Linux and macOS Claude Code refuses --dangerously-skip-permissions / bypassPermissions when running as root or under sudo ('cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons'); the check is skipped inside a 'recognized sandbox'.
observed_method: observe: run -p --dangerously-skip-permissions as uid 0 and as uid 1000 in the container; capture exit code and stderr
notes: Docs do not name how a sandbox is recognized; IS_SANDBOX is not in the env-var reference or CHANGELOG, so it is not used here.

documented_claim: permissions.defaultMode bypassPermissions or auto in project or local settings does not take effect (bypass ignored from project/local since v2.1.257).
observed_method: observe: synthetic repo with .claude/settings.json {"permissions":{"defaultMode":"bypassPermissions"}}; read permissionMode from stream-json init

documented_claim: Session transcripts are stored in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays); --no-session-persistence or CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1 skip writing them.
observed_method: observe: file-watch after -p runs with and without --no-session-persistence; record paths and modes under ~/.claude (projects/, file-history/, history.jsonl, session-env/)
notes: Host structure (names/modes only, 2026-10-15): transcripts 0600, history.jsonl 0600, ~/.claude 0755. (One state-file observation is held privately pending disclosure.)

documented_claim: Auto memory is on by default in local sessions and lives at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ (MEMORY.md); CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 or autoMemoryEnabled:false turns it off; project CLAUDE.md is loaded as instructions (not by --bare).
observed_method: observe: synthetic repo CLAUDE.md with inert canary instruction (reply token); run -p; check reply token and whether a memory/ dir is written; repeat with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1

documented_claim: Built-in subagents inherit the parent conversation's permission rules; project subagent frontmatter hooks and inline mcpServers are not used under -p in a never-trusted folder (since 2.1.218).
observed_method: observe: synthetic .claude/agents/probe.md with a frontmatter hook touching /tmp/canary-agent and an inline stdio mcpServer; -p prompt asks to use the agent; expect neither canary
notes: Small local models may not invoke the subagent reliably; record N/A (model) if the Agent tool is never called.
